headline: Built sequences get a bin of their own, and Settings shows where things will go.
notes: Stringouts and unused-span sequences now go into a _STRINGOUTS bin – inside the bin the clips came from, or at the top of the project – and the subclips of unused spans go in with them, so they no longer show up as clips left to try

A stringout no longer counts as using a clip: building one from Not in this cut leaves the list as it was, a clip only in a stringout says so, and the Project view tags it STRINGOUT ONLY. Drop a stringout into a real sequence and its clips count again
The bin view keeps comparing with your cut after Build stringout opens the new sequence, and Hide old folds stringouts away in a clip's list
Settings shows a green line under File unused into and Built sequences land, naming the exact bin the current setting sends things to
Each build gets a sub-bin of its own inside _STRINGOUTS, named for the clip or bin it came from (Interview_A_STRINGOUT), and a second build from the same source lands in the same one
The Archive tab in Settings is now called Organisation, and its Building sequences group is now Stringout sequences
Clip labels are always shown – the setting that hid them has gone
Clip tags has moved up into Settings › Panel › How rows look, under Times
The ×2 badge has gone from the Used and Not used lists – beside the use count it read as a second one. In Duplicate imports each file now says how many items it has, for example 2 items
Imported twice is now called Duplicate imports
Ticking rows in Duplicate imports and pressing Move files them into _DUPLICATE IMPORTS, the way Offline files into _OFFLINE, and Put back brings them home
Pointing at Move, Put back or Delete empty bins now shows the count and undo cost in the status line, and Move its merged-clip warning
A setting's confirmation now shows inside the Settings window, not hidden behind it
Settings › Panel shows how your rows will look, and changes as you change Detail, Times and Clip tags
Point at a group heading in Settings to see what that group is for, and each tab has its own line at the foot
Label picker is now Show / Hide, with an eye on each
Pressing Activate twice, or while it is greyed out, no longer uses up a second licence seat
The update banner comes back after a restart instead of waiting a day
The first tour no longer ends early when you open the Project view and come back
Pressing Move, Put back or Send twice in a row no longer runs it twice
A clip or bin name starting with = in an exported CSV can no longer run as a spreadsheet formula
